title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: Objection 7 — judicial law vs war; tip before God-as-judge
pass_a_gloss: Seventh: imputation of sin and infliction of penalty are judicial actions. They ought to be done by a judge according to laws. And the law is: The soul that has sinned, it shall die. The father shall not bear the son's iniquity, nor the son the father's. On the contrary in war the laws are silent, and, as in a disturbed state, all things are done by force: nor is the end that justice be done, but victory, for whose sake the people on whom war is made are intent on this one thing—to harm the one making it. And since the King's power lies in the multitude and wealth of subjects, they strive to wear down, diminish, and overthrow it by spoiling the King's subjects of strength and goods and life. But God, when he imputes sin to men and exercises vengeance, plays a Judge's part. Tip before the eighth objection (Adam not actually father or in relation when he sinned) deepen.
pass_b_english: Seventh. To impute sin and to inflict a penalty are acts of a court. A judge must do them according to laws. And the law runs: The soul that has sinned shall itself die. A father shall not bear a son's iniquity, nor a son a father's. War is another regime: laws fall silent, and, as in a broken order, all things are done by force; nor is the end that justice be done, but victory—for whose sake the people under attack work only to harm the one who makes war. Because a King's strength sits in his subjects' numbers and wealth, they try to grind that strength down, diminish it, and overthrow it by stripping subjects of force and goods and life: both to vex the King and hurt him, and to save themselves and grow richer. God, when he charges men with sin and takes vengeance, does not play that war-game: he takes a Judge's part.
source_text: Septimo, peccati imputatio, & poenae inflictio, actiones sunt judiciariae. Fieri debent a judice secundum leges. Lex autem est, Anima quae peccaverit ipsa morietur. Non feret iniquitatem filii pater, nec patris filius. Contra in bello leges silent, &, ut in statu perturbato, omnia vi fiunt: nec finis est ut fiat justitia, sed victoria, cuius causa gens cui bellum infertur in id unum intenta est, ut inferenti incommodet. Quoniam autem Regis potentia in subditorum multitudine & opibus sita est, eam ut atterant, & imminuant, & evertant, subditos Regi pro viribus, & bonis, & vita spoliare conantur: in quo scopus est & regi aegre facere, illique incommodare, & se tueri, ac opibus augere. Deus vero cum peccatum hominibus imputat & vindictam exercet, Judicis partibus fungitur.
